title: Bicentennial State Department tour: Istanbul, Iran, Pakistan
summary: Edison tells of being picked with Benny Carter's group to tour the Middle East, seeing Istanbul, Ankara, Tehran, Isfahan, Shiraz and Karachi.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So during the Bicentennial, the American government, they asked -- five musicians were chosen, I was one of the five, to do a tour of the Middle East, you know, and Cleopatra has always been one of my favorite rulers, you know. She was in an age where I think it was absolutely just fabulous back in those days, you know. So I was one of the five to be

to take a trip to the iiiddle East asked by Benny Carter/and I couldn't wait, because I never dreamed I would go to a country that I couldn't even spell the word when I was going -- one of my words I -- Constantinople. We went to Turkey -- they changed it to Turkey.
Well, they call it Istanbul.
Yeah, Istanbul, yeah. We went to Istabul, right from here to Istanbul, from Los Angeles.
That's one of the funny things, you know, how people heard, you know, they heard this is obviously saying Constantinople, but the Turks were / Istanbul.

Istanbul, right. Istanbul, Constantinople. And you know, when you get off the plane over there, you're in a different world. It looks like wherever you left, you never think of it anymore because there's nothing there that reminds you of here in North America and went to Istanbul and what a thrill. What a thrill. Oh, I took a tour of the Bosporus, you know, the Dardanelles.
Yeah, yeah.
Went to the Blue Mosque. I saw St. Sophia, the chapel there. Oh, it's -- you know, it's just amazing. It's indescribable.
And then you went on to --
To Ankara from there.
And Iran, too, didn't you?
Yeah, then we left Ankara and went to Iran, see? Went to Tehran, Isfahan, just beautiful, just beautiful, Shiraz. Then we came back to -- we stayed at a hotel

called the Shah Habaz. I've never seen such work of art in a hotel. That's where the Shah built it for his guests, you know. And it's just indescribable, you know, and the domes on the universities, you know, like the Turkish domes with all those colors. When the sun would shine on that dome, it was absolutely just -- you just couldn't describe the colors. Then we went from there to Tehran to Karachi --

Then we went from Karachi to Islamabad, Islamabad to Rawalpindi. Then from there to --
Oh, in India.
No, that's in Karachi.

Pakistan, right.
Well, that was interesting, too, wasn't it?
